Part 1 · Fundamentals

Why boil biodiesel under vacuum, and why must a batch be cut?

Design charge 110 L = 95.7 kg (project report, Table 2)

Four lumps of methyl esters

Boiling points from the model's vapour-pressure lines (assumed anchors). Feed B is the Table 9 charge measured at the plant.

The thermal limit sets the pressure

At one atmosphere the esters degrade before they boil

1013 mbar

The charge would boil near : oxidation, colour, polymer.

170 mbar pot

The charge boils at ; the pot ends near 269 °C.

53 mbar pilot

Cooler still, but the vapour is so thin the packing floods.

Alarm TIC-101 at 280 °C; trip TSHH-101 at 290 °C.

Derivation · vapour pressure of one ester

From the Clapeyron equation to a straight line in 1/T

The thermal limit needs boiling points at any pressure.

$P^{sat}$
vapour pressure of the pure ester
mbar
$\Delta H_v$
heat of vaporisation (assumed 77–99)
kJ/mol
$T_{ref}$
boiling point at the anchor $P_{ref}$ = 160 mbar
K
$\dfrac{dP^{sat}}{dT}=\dfrac{\Delta H_v}{T\,\Delta v}$Clapeyron: equilibrium along the boiling line
$\dfrac{d\ln P^{sat}}{dT}=\dfrac{\Delta H_v}{RT^2}$$\Delta v\approx RT/P$: liquid volume neglected
$\ln\dfrac{P^{sat}}{P_{ref}}=-\dfrac{\Delta H_v}{R}\left(\dfrac1T-\dfrac1{T_{ref}}\right)$integrate with constant $\Delta H_v$

Interactive · set the pressure

Each 10 × less pressure buys about 60 °C

Clausius–Clapeyron$\ln\frac{P^{sat}}{P_{ref}}=-\frac{\Delta H_v}{R}\left(\frac1T-\frac1{T_{ref}}\right)$

At 160 mbar C16:0 boils at 250 °C; at 1013 mbar the model puts it at 300 °C.

Derivation · a mixture boils at its bubble point

Raoult's law sets the pot temperature

The pot holds a mixture, not one ester.

$x_i,\ y_i$
mole fraction of lump $i$ in liquid, in vapour
–
$P$
pot pressure (PI-103)
mbar
$\alpha_{ij}$
relative volatility of $i$ to $j$
–
$y_iP=x_iP_i^{sat}(T)$ideal liquid: Raoult's law per lump
$\sum_i x_iP_i^{sat}(T_b)=P$vapour fractions sum to one: solve for $T_b$
$\alpha_{ij}=P_i^{sat}/P_j^{sat}$ratio of vapour to liquid enrichment

Interactive · move through the campaign, change the pot pressure

The pot gets heavier, so it boils hotter

Bubble point$\sum_i x_iP_i^{sat}(T_b)=P$

At 170 mbar the pot rises from 255 to 269 °C as C16:0 leaves; the pressure moves it more.

Relative volatility at the charge bubble point, 170 mbar

Neighbouring esters differ by a factor of only 2 to 3

C14 / C16:0 α =

Sets how cleanly the off-cut removes the lights.

Derivation · the still with no column

The Rayleigh balance of a batch still

Batch means no steady state: the still composition moves.

$W,\ W_0$
moles left in the still; at the start
mol
$x_W,\ y$
still liquid, and the vapour leaving it
–
$d(Wx_W)=y\,dW$what leaves the still is vapour of composition $y$
$\dfrac{dW}{W}=\dfrac{dx_W}{y-x_W}$expand and divide by $W(y-x_W)$
$\ln\dfrac{W_0}{W}=\displaystyle\int_{x_W}^{x_{W0}}\frac{dx}{y-x}$integrate; $y=\alpha x/(1+(\alpha-1)x)$ for two lumps

Interactive · boil off part of a C16:0 / C18 mixture with no column

One stage cannot make 99 % product

Rayleigh$\ln\frac{W_0}{W}=\int\frac{dx}{y-x}$

At α 2.2 the first vapour is only about 70 % C16:0: a column with reflux must multiply the stages.

Constant-reflux batch distillation

One charge, three products, four phases

The column gives many stages; reflux decides how hard they work.

1 · Total reflux

Lights gather at the top; nothing is drawn.

2 · Off-cut, R 15

Lights to TK-201 until D-105 shows below 4 %.

3 · Product cut, R 10

C16:0 to TK-202 at 99 wt %.

4 · End

Stop before the C18 front; the residue stays in the pot.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Vacuum keeps the pot below the degradation limit.
  • The pot boils at its bubble point, which rises through the batch.
  • α of 2–3 needs many stages and high reflux.
  • A batch is run as cuts: total reflux, off-cut, product, end.

Derivation · minimum stages at total reflux

Fenske counts the stages a split needs

Times come from duty and R; purity comes from the stages.

$x_D,\ x_B$
key-lump fraction at the top, at the bottom
–
$N_{min}$
equilibrium stages at total reflux
–
$\dfrac{x_D}{1-x_D}=\alpha^{N_{min}}\dfrac{x_B}{1-x_B}$each stage multiplies the ratio by α
$N_{min}=\dfrac{\ln\!\left[\frac{x_D}{1-x_D}\cdot\frac{1-x_B}{x_B}\right]}{\ln\alpha}$take logarithms; constant α assumed

Interactive · pick a split and its purities

Twenty stages against what each split needs

Fenske$N_{min}=\ln\!\left[\frac{x_D}{1-x_D}\frac{1-x_B}{x_B}\right]/\ln\alpha$

C16:0 / C18 at 99 % / 1 % needs 11.6 stages; 20 installed give the margin a finite R needs.

Derivation · why vacuum makes the packing flood

Thin vapour moves fast

$\rho_v$
vapour density at the pot
kg/m³
$u,\ F$
vapour velocity; capacity factor
m/s, Pa0.5
$FL$
flooding index (model)
%
$\rho_v=PM/RT$ideal gas: 1.06 kg/m³ at 170 mbar
$F=u\sqrt{\rho_v}\ \Rightarrow\ u\propto V/\rho_v$same mass flow, lower density: faster
$FL=58\,\%\cdot\dfrac{V}{38}\sqrt{\dfrac{165}{P}}$model form: flooding grows as $V/\sqrt P$

Duty and pressure share one flooding budget

CaseBoil-upFlooding
Design, 3 kW at 160 mbar40 kg/h61 %
Efficiency starts to fallabove 80 %
Liquid carried upwardabove 95 %

Flooding grows with boil-up and with lower pressure (Design tab, operating window).

E-103 on tempered water

The condenser water must stay warm

Area

$A=Q/(U\,\Delta T_{lm})$ ≈ 0.11 m² at 150 W/m²K.

Water

$\dot m=Q/(c_p\Delta T)$ ≈ 0.86 m³/h at 3 K; 1.2 m³/h fitted.

Above 45 °C

C16 and C18 esters freeze at 30–38 °C on cold tubes.

Design 60 °C; alarms TI-109 at 45 and 80 °C.

Interactive · pick a decision

Every choice answers a property of the esters

Vacuum, packing, warm water and duty control all follow from heat-sensitive, high-boiling esters.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Duty fixes boil-up; R fixes the draw and the cut times.
  • The C16:0 / C18 split needs 11.6 stages minimum; 20 are fitted.
  • Vacuum thins the vapour: duty is capped by flooding.
  • Tempered water at 60 °C keeps the esters liquid in E-103.

Part 3 · Operation

How is one campaign run, from total reflux to the end of the product cut?

Part 3 · the plan

The campaign, phase by phase

  1. Start-up orderutilities before heat
  2. The reference campaignwhat the column does over 15 hours
  3. Cut pointsa sample for the switch, the front for the end
  4. Choosing Rrecovery against productivity
  5. Shutdowncool under vacuum, then break it

Design tab · order of the operating conditions

Cooling and vacuum come before any heat

  1. Tempered water on, above 45 °C.
  2. VP-101 on; PIC-102 to 160 mbar.
  3. Hot oil to 290 °C; arm heating.
  4. Heat up at up to 8 kW; cut to 3 kW before boiling.
  5. Drum level and reflux in AUTO; hold total reflux.

Process tab · expert run on the design charge

Fifteen hours, three products

Model, noise off. Aspen design case of the project: switch 271 min, end 771 min, 32.5 kg, 2.53 kg/h.

Temperatures, receivers and the drum over 907 minutes

Interactive · full campaigns on the model

Higher R recovers more C16:0, but slowly

Product-cut R

Charge

R 6 gives 2.91 kg/h at 74.6 % recovery; R 10 gives 2.29 kg/h at 80.6 %: the project chose recovery.

Graded procedure · normal shutdown and cool-down

Cool under vacuum, then break it with N₂

  1. HS-107 CLOSED: total reflux.
  2. Heater off; HV-104 oil cooler open, TV-101 wide open.
  3. Keep VP-101 and P-108 until the pot is below 150 °C.
  4. Stop P-104; disarm heating.
  5. Break vacuum with N₂ (HV-110); stop the pumps.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Water and vacuum first; heat last, and cut to 3 kW before boiling.
  • Switch to the product cut on the D-105 sample result.
  • End on the TK-202 composite; TI-103 warns of the front.
  • Cool below 150 °C under vacuum before N₂ breaks it.

Part 4 · summary

What part 4 settled

  • Eight blocks around one packed column.
  • Streams change through the batch: compare moments.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Hold the pressure: it sets every boiling point and keeps the esters below degradation.

2

Set the duty for boil-up and stay inside the flooding window.

3

Switch on the sample, stop on the composite, watch the C18 front.

4

Close every balance on inventories: a batch only moves its charge.

5

Keep water and vacuum on whenever the pot is hot.
